title: Moonshot AI's Kimi big shot appears in a maid outfit at the 2026 Cloud Bridge Conference, suspected of cosplaying as DeepSeek's Big Fat Fish

content_html:
Another amusing cross-industry stunt has been added to the AI world. On November 19, the 2026 Cloud Bridge Conference was held at Grand Canal Hanggang Park in Gongshu, Hangzhou, and a photo from the roundtable discussion sparked heated discussion online. In the photo, Tang Feihu, a senior R&D engineer and developer relations lead for Moonshot AI's Kimi, was speaking with a microphone in hand while wearing a silver-blue wig and a blue-and-white maid outfit.

Roundtable Look Draws Attention: Kimi Engineer Apparently Dressed as DeepSeek's "Big Fat Fish"

Footage from the scene showed that Tang Feihu's outfit that day appeared to be inspired by "Big Fat Fish," the anthropomorphic persona of large-model maker DeepSeek, also nicknamed "Whale Girl" by netizens. As an R&D staffer in a competitor's camp, choosing to dress up as another large-model company's image while speaking on stage created a striking contrast that quickly caught many netizens' attention. After the photo spread, some joked, "One look and you can tell he's a big shot," while others wondered why he had chosen another large-model company's image as inspiration for his look.

A Veteran ACG Fan: The Community Lore of "Kojima Minako" and "Dao Niang"

For developers familiar with Tang Feihu, this outfit was not really surprising. He has long loved ACG culture and, in his early years, appeared publicly in a long-haired, feminine outfit. Even when invited to tech events, he once used a photo of himself in women's clothing as the image for his guest introduction.

In programmer circles, Tang Feihu also has a well-known nickname: "Kojima Minako." Some also call him "Dao Niang," or "Island Girl." As early as 2016, an introduction for a programming experience-sharing event aimed at student developers already used "Dao Niang" to refer to this tech competitor, who had won the overall championship in Microsoft's "Beauty of Programming" challenge.

From Competition-Based Admission to Algorithm Ace: A Full Look at His Hardcore Resume

Behind his ACG hobby and personal style, Tang Feihu has a very solid computer science and algorithms background:

Education and Taking a Leave to Start a Business: According to a 2015 interview with him by China Science Daily, while studying at Hefei No. 1 High School, he participated in computer competitions and was admitted to Harbin Institute of Technology's Software Engineering program based on his competition results. Just three months after enrolling in 2010, because he had already encountered some of the course content in high school, he chose to take a leave of absence and joined a startup team formed by his high school classmates. In August 2012, he returned to HIT, focusing on algorithms and data structures, and later taught algorithm courses for the school's training team.

Competition Honors and Project Experience: In 2014, Tang Feihu won gold medals at the ACM International Collegiate Programming Contest Beijing and Mudanjiang sites. Later, in Microsoft's 2015 "Beauty of Programming" challenge, he teamed up with Guo Xiaoxu, a contestant from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, to develop an intelligent travel information query assistant. The program could identify departure locations from users' natural-language input, convert times, and distinguish whether the query was about plane tickets, train tickets, or attraction tickets. The two won first prize with this project.

Career Path: After leaving campus and the competition stage, Tang Feihu worked as an engineer at Google Shanghai. Today, he does R&D at Moonshot AI and leads developer relations.
